newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - Wienerberger sees boost from property deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wienerberger sees boost from property deal.

text.p: The world's biggest brickmaker, Austria's Wienerberger, said on Thursday it had sold a major Vienna office complex for three billion schillings ($251.8 million) in a deal that analysts said would strongly boost group earnings.

Wienerberger Baustoffindustrie sold Business Park Vienna, the capital's largest business centre with some 86,500 square metres of usable space, to property management group Immofinanz, realising a net gain of 500 million schillings.

"This deal marks a milestone in the strategic development of Wienerberger group and enables us to concentrate on our core businesses -- bricks and pipes," chief executive Schaschl told a news conference.
"A gain of 500 million schillings paves the way for big steps forward," he added.
The company said it aimed to expand its core businesses in Eastern Europe and also develop new activities in construction to counter the current crisis in the sector across Europe.
As part of the deal, Wienerberger bought an almost 12 percent stake in Immofinanz, one of Austria's leading real estate units, for 150 million schillings in cash.

"This is a good investment for us because Immofinanz's average profitability in the last five years after taxes was 7.4 percent," Schaschl told Reuters. Wienerberger is now the largest private shareholder in Immofinanz, which is managed by unlisted Constantia Privatbank.
Wienerberger said the deal with Immofinanz would contribute significantly to earnings growth in the current year.
"We will increase our pre-tax profit by at least 25 percent and our turnover, excluding this project, by 10 percent," Schaschl said.
Wienerberger posted a drop in 1996 pre-tax profit to 1.37 billion schillings from 1.495 billion the year before, while group sales rose to 15.06 billion schillings last year from 12.86 billion.
"The first quarter has not been very good but was much better than last year and shows we are well on track to come close to our profit target for this year," Schaschl said.
Immofinanz would register an increase in rental income of about 300 million schillings this year, Schaschl noted.
Analysts hailed the deal as positive for Wienerberger and said it would lay the ground for further acquisitions.

"This was a successful project that sold for a good price and will have a good influence on 1997 results," said Wolfgang Pinner, analyst at Investment Bank Austria. He added he had raised his earnings per share estimate for 1997 to 150 from 121 schillings.
Another analyst at an Austrian bank said she was surprised by the deal but regarded it as positive and had increased her 1997 earnings estimates to 162 schillings per share from 120.
Analysts on Wednesday widely predicted Wienerberger was poised to announce a sale of its Treibacher chemicals and abrasive materials unit.
Wienerberger is majority controlled by Austria's Creditanstalt and Belgium's Koramic.
Wienerberger shares were up one schilling at 2,335 in midday trading in an otherwise bearish Austrian market. ($ = 11.91 Austrian Schillings)
